findings.title: `tape_complete_through` is documented as "the newest stored trade" — the exact phrasing the schema comment was rewritten to remove
findings.description:
`TradesResponse.tape_complete_through` carries `Field(description="Created time of the newest stored trade. Null means the trades phase has never run — not that the tape is empty today.")`. That is the inverse of what the field holds. It is populated from `TradesResponse.build(... facts.tape_complete_through ...)`, which `serve_timeseries.tape_facts` fills with `sync_state['trades'].watermark_ts` — the end of the last fully walked window, which is typically *later* than the newest stored trade because quiet periods produce no rows.

The project has an explicit, mechanically enforced stance that this phrasing is wrong: `src/manta_trading/market/schema/migrations/kalshi.py` (kalshi_006) rewrites the column comment to "the tape is complete through this instant (end of the last fully walked window) - NOT the newest stored trade (slice 265, Decision 1)", and `test/integration/test_kalshi_migrations.py:533` asserts the string `"created_time of the newest stored trade"` is **absent** from that comment. Slice design D5 restates the same thing.

The consequence is not cosmetic: D5 exists so a `count: 0` is unambiguous. A client reading "newest stored trade" interprets the field as a *floor on stored rows* rather than a *ceiling on completeness*, and will read a legitimately quiet window as a collection gap — the precise misreading D5 was written to prevent. Since the value is correct and only the description is wrong, this is a doc defect, but it is on the published contract of the field the slice singles out.

Two related sites repeat the same claim and should be corrected together:
- `src/manta_trading/data/kalshi/serve_timeseries.py#tape_facts` — module-level docstring opens "The trades tape's floor and its newest stored trade."
- `README.md:621` (outside this diff, but it is the same sentence and ships to consumers).

For contrast, `coverage_from`'s description ("Oldest instant the trades tape reaches, across the live and historical surfaces") is accurate.

findings.title: The trades re-nesting is positional and untyped, so a new stored column would be fetched and silently dropped
findings.description:
`TradeRecord.from_row` reads `values[0]` … `values[7]` positionally, and `TradeRow.values` is declared `tuple[Any, ...]` (`src/manta_trading/data/kalshi/serve_timeseries.py#TradeRow`). `fetch_trades` selects `TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS`, derived from `TRADE_COLUMNS`, so adding a column to `TRADE_COLUMNS` widens the fetched tuple without changing the mapping code — the extra value is read, ignored, and never served, with no error anywhere.

The candle path deliberately does not have this property (its docstring: "a column added there is served here without an edit"), and the unit tests defend it structurally — `test/unit/api_server/test_kalshi_models.py::TestCandleRecord::test_nested_field_set_is_exactly_what_candle_columns_describes` asserts the served field set equals the set `CANDLE_COLUMNS` describes.

There is no analogous assertion for trades, and the integration test that looks like one cannot catch it: `test/integration/test_kalshi_serving.py::TestTradeWindow::test_value_count_matches_the_repository_mapping` asserts `len(r.values) == len(TRADE_COLUMNS) - 1`, which auto-adjusts to whatever `TRADE_COLUMNS` becomes, so it passes for 8 values or 9. The `Any` element type is what removes the last line of defence (a typed tuple or a `TRADE_COLUMNS`-driven mapping would make the omission a type error or a test failure).

findings.title: `_admit_rows` is duplicated verbatim between the two Kalshi route modules
findings.description:
`_admit_rows` exists in `src/manta_trading/api_server/routes/kalshi_catalog.py#_admit_rows` and is copied into the new `kalshi_timeseries.py` with the same body, the same docstring, the same `count > max_rows` comparison, and the same `HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT` code. Only the trailing advice differs (`"narrow the filter"` vs `"narrow start/end"`), which is a parameter, not a reason to fork the function.

This is the rule the project states most plainly ("Do not duplicate logic. Respect DRY"; "Never scatter comparison values across code … define it once"), and it is the same shape the slice already got right elsewhere — `serialization.timeseries_response` and `routes/windows.resolve_window` were both extracted precisely because a second consumer appeared. The ceiling comparison now has two definition sites free to drift: a change to the comparison (e.g. `>=`) or to the status code must be made twice, and nothing fails if only one is made.

findings.title: `windows.py`'s own justification applies to `gaps.py`, which was left with its own copy
findings.description:
`windows.py`'s module docstring argues that the day-boundary convention "lives here rather than in `bars.py` because two route families now depend on it, and two derivations of 'the last instant of a day' is exactly how one of them ends up exclusive by accident." After this change, "midnight UTC on a date" is still spelled three times: `windows.window_start_utc`, `src/manta_trading/api_server/routes/gaps.py:54` (`_window_start_utc`, byte-identical body), and `src/manta_trading/data/gaps/repair_921.py#window_start_utc`.

The `gaps.py` **end** bound is genuinely different and correctly left alone — it returns next-midnight because its predicate is half-open (`gap_start < %s`), and its docstring explains that with a production measurement. The **start** bound is not different. This is a note rather than a concern because `gaps.py`'s pair is documented and self-consistent, and folding it in would widen the diff; but the new module's stated rationale is only half-applied, so the next route author has two precedents to choose from.

findings.title: `_window`'s `extra` parameter is period-specific despite its generic name and untyped contract
findings.description: `_window(..., extra: dict[str, Any] | None = None)` merges `extra` into the bound parameters *and* uses `if extra:` to decide whether to append the literal clause `period = %(period)s`. Any future caller that passes an `extra` for a different purpose gets a `period` predicate with no bound parameter, which psycopg rejects at execute time — a confusing failure for a call that looks reasonable at the call site. Both current callers pass exactly `{"period": period}`, so nothing is broken today; naming the parameter `period` (and typing it `int | None`) would make the contract match the behaviour, or a `sql.SQL` fragment parameter would remove the implicit coupling entirely.

findings.title: Duplicated invariant check and message for the malformed trades state row
findings.description: `tape_facts` re-implements the guard and repeats the message string verbatim from `src/manta_trading/data/kalshi/trade_status.py#read_trade_status`: `"kalshi.sync_state['trades'] exists without a watermark or coverage floor; the row is written only by the trades phase's init_state"`. Both modules already import `STATE_QUERY` and `effective_tape_floor` from `trade_status`, so a shared `_require_trades_state(row)` helper (or a small accessor) would sit naturally beside the function the slice deliberately promoted for exactly this reason. The duplicated string means a future rewording of the diagnostic has two sites, and only one is likely to be found.

findings.title: Load-test constants restated as literals beside their definitions
findings.description: The test asserts `body["count"] == 450` while `KALSHI_MARKET_COUNT = 450` is defined in `test/load/conftest.py` and the module already imports four sibling constants (`KALSHI_DENSE_EVENT`, `KALSHI_DENSE_MARKET`, `KALSHI_SERIES`, `KALSHI_START`) from it — so the derived-from-one-place pattern is established one line away. The same theme appears in `test/load/conftest.py#_seed_kalshi_dense`: the candlestick `COPY` column list is derived from `CANDLE_COLUMNS`, while the trades `COPY` column list is hardcoded, so a change to `TRADE_COLUMNS` would leave the fixture seeding a stale shape (and the assertion above unable to notice). The `24_382` literal in `test_events_list_at_production_width` is fine — it is a production measurement with its provenance in the docstring, not a restatement of a fixture constant.

findings.title: The refusal ordering and the tape-filter derivation are implemented as designed and defended against real code paths
findings.description:
Two properties the design leans on are actually true in the code, not just asserted in prose.

The over-ceiling refusal is raised by `_admit_rows` *after* `await loop.run_in_executor(...)` returns, so the `with pool.connection()` block has already closed on every path — including the 404, which is raised inside the block and unwound through it. `test/unit/api_server/test_kalshi_timeseries.py::TestCeiling::test_the_connection_is_released_before_the_refusal` asserts this against a pool that counts open checkouts, and the load test's `_RecordingCursor` proves the stronger claim (no row-projecting `SELECT` against `kalshi.trades`) against a real database rather than a mock.

`tape_filtered` does not re-spell the comparison: it renders `trades_filter_sql(excluded)` and evaluates the same parameter set, and `test/integration/test_kalshi_serving.py::TestTapeFiltered` executes the rendered SQL *and* the Python helper across five configurations, asserting they agree — so the two cannot drift silently. `effective_tape_floor`'s promotion is likewise complete (no `_effective_floor` remains anywhere in `src/` or `test/`) and its three branches are covered directly in `test/integration/test_kalshi_status.py::TestEffectiveTapeFloor`.

structured_findings.summary: `tape_complete_through` is documented as "the newest stored trade" — the exact phrasing the schema comment was rewritten to remove
The trades re-nesting is positional and untyped, so a new stored column would be fetched and silently dropped
`_admit_rows` is duplicated verbatim between the two Kalshi route modules
`windows.py`'s own justification applies to `gaps.py`, which was left with its own copy
`_window`'s `extra` parameter is period-specific despite its generic name and untyped contract
Duplicated invariant check and message for the malformed trades state row
Load-test constants restated as literals beside their definitions
The refusal ordering and the tape-filter derivation are implemented as designed and defended against real code paths
